name: PPO
summary: PPO constrains each policy update with a clipped surrogate objective, capturing most of the stability of trust-region methods at a fraction of the implementation complexity. In robotics it became the default algorithm for massively parallel simulation training: locomotion, in-hand manipulation and sim-to-real dexterity pipelines almost all run PPO over thousands of parallel environments.
innovation: Clipped surrogate objective giving trust-region-like stability with first-order optimization.
Robust to hyperparameters across wildly different tasks, which is why it survived.
matters: The algorithm actually running inside Isaac Lab, sim-to-real dexterity, and RLHF alike.
limits: On-policy and therefore sample-hungry: impractical to run directly on real hardware.
lineage: Root of the on-policy branch used for sim-trained manipulation.
